headline: Union Minister Vaishnaw outlines India's semiconductor roadmap to 2035
summary: Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw stated at the NDTV World Summit that India aims to progress from 28-nanometre to 3-nanometre chip manufacturing by 2035. The roadmap focuses on legacy nodes first to counter global supply-chain concentration before advancing to complex technologies under Semicon 2.0. India currently has 15 semiconductor plants, with five in commercial production and exports already reaching Japan, the US, and Europe. The government also targets domestic mobile phone branding and design capabilities by October 2028. For retail investors, this signals long-term policy support for domestic electronics manufacturing, component suppliers, and ATMP facilities.
whats_next: Semicon 2.0 rollout and execution of the Tata fabrication project at Tolera
why_it_matters: Long-term policy tailwinds for domestic semiconductor and electronics manufacturing stocks
winners_losers: Domestic chip and electronics manufacturers gain / legacy importers hurt
